lead: # build.rs parses the committed graph store directly — see crates/graph-materialize/build.rs.
# `bsc-emit` — materialize retired modules from their packaged seeds into the generated tree.
# DELIBERATELY LEAN, and that is the whole reason this is its own crate rather than a module inside
# `bsc-ui`. It runs from the BUILD TREE — seven npm entries and the vite plugin — and on CI, where the
# frontend job is Node-only today. Linking it into `bsc` alone would mean the frontend CI job had to
# build `bsc`, which pulls `bsc-data` and so bundled DuckDB: CLAUDE.md measures a first
# `cargo build -p bsc --bin bsc` at 343s plus ~1.8 GB of C++ output. Paying that on every frontend PR
# to run a file-copying step is not defensible.
# `bsc-record` is a three-dependency crate (serde_json, regex, bsc-util) with no DuckDB, no arrow and
# no tree-sitter, so a binary over it builds in a fraction of that. Same reason `bsc-agent` and
sections.name: [build-dependencies]

lead: # The BUILD-TREE entry point. `bsc ui emit records` is the agent-facing door over the same lib; this
# one exists so `npm run typecheck` never has to link DuckDB.
sections.name: [[bin]]
